Source: http://www.norml.org.nz

Posted September 14, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: As I keep saying, marijuana prohibition is not just a failure. It is a counterproductive fraud -- that is actually making the very real problems of substance misuse and abuse worse than they would otherwise become. This is particularly true of its impact on children.
See
How the War On Marijuana To Save The Children
Has Become A War On the Children To Save Marijuana Prohibition

However, many sincere prohibitionists simply cannot grasp that concept. Consequently, the worse the fiasco created by marijuana prohibition, the more they love it. New Zealand prohibitionists are in a state of near hysteria over the fact that the government is going to look at the possibility of considering the option of thinking about a review of the laws.

Sadly, this Cassandra chorus’ loudest voices are the school principals. They claim that even thinking about reducing penalties for adult marijuana users " sends the wrong message to children " that it would be good for them to stay stoned all day at school.
See
Do New Zealand Educators Have Any Intellectual Standards? Is Their Ideology More Important Than Their Students? Weigh the Evidence. That Is More Than They Do.

This is an intellectually indefensible argument, unless one is prepared to eliminate all distinctions between adults and children. However, in fairness to them, they are not unique in this. Indeed, prominent educators in DEAland have made similar arguments.
See
Rochester Institute Of Technology Won't Recognize Cannabis Coalition -
Fears It " will encourage dangerous criminal elements. "

Consequently, marijuana is blamed for the problems created by marijuana prohibition, and so the worse the problems created by marijuana prohibition become, the more these very problems are cited as justification for more of the same. And the greater the resistance becomes even to considering change.)

Press Release: New Zealand National Party

Drugs Already Affecting Education
September 14, 2000

Yet another warning bell has sounded for the Government on decriminalisation of cannabis, but they still aren't listening, National Education spokesperson Nick Smith said today.

" The latest school suspension figures show for the first time drugs are now the leading cause of suspensions. 1505 students were suspended for drugs, accounting for 30% of suspensions. This is testament to the difficulties talk about the decriminalisation of cannabis is causing our schools.

" When the Minister of Education, Prime Minister, Health Minister and Youth Affairs Minister are publicly supporting decriminalisation of the drug it sends a strong message to our young people that the drug is okay.

" We want young people in school learning, not smoking dope.

See
Legalize Marijuana and Improve High-School Academic Performance? Holland Ranks First – The US Very Low

" Principals and Boards are pleading with the Government to stop any plans to decriminalise the drug. Youth Parliamentarians voted against it. Suspension figures show what uncertainty about the drug has done. I hate to think how many more suspensions there will be if the Government has its way and cannabis is decriminalised.

" The effect the uncertainty created by the Government is having on students is patently obvious. Today's announcement that a six-month select committee inquiry will go ahead will only make matters worse, " Dr Smith said.

See
California Bureaucracy Suppresses Report Showing Marijuana Use Among California Students Leveled Off After Passage Of Prop 215. Meanwhile, In New Zealand, Prohbitionists Use The Same Party Line.

Ends

(MarijuanaNews note: The following press release makes the sad, but basic point that there cannot be a full and fair revue of the impact of either marijuana use or marijuana prohibition while people are afraid to speak out. That fact alone should make people think twice about marijuana prohibition.)

Coalition Calls For Moratorium On Cannabis Arrests
September 14, 2000,
Press Release: Coalition for Cannabis Law Reform

Coalition Calls For A Moratorium On Cannabis Arrests While Review Takes Place

The Coalition for Cannabis Law Reform today welcomed the government's announcement of the terms of reference for the first inquiry into the health effects and legal status of cannabis since 1973. The Coalition has called for a moratorium on arrests for personal amounts of cannabis in light of this announcement.

The Coalition will be writing to the Health Select Committee chair, Judy Keall and Prime Minister Helen Clark, asking that they recognise that the current threat of arrest and imprisonment for cannabis possession will act as a deterrent to those who might wish to discuss the health effects associated with their own cannabis use.

The Coalition estimates that the police will arrest and prosecute some 6000 cannabis users between now and the closing date for submissions in February 2001. The coalition believes that this represents a considerable deterrent to the estimated half a million regular cannabis users from becoming involved in this debate.

(MarijuanaNews note: New Zealand may well have the highest marijuana arrest rate in the world, and the burden falls most heavily on the indigenous Maori minority. They are 5 times as likely to be arrested and 20 times as likely to be jailed on marijuana charges as the European Kiwi majority.)
See
Founder of New Zealand NORML Calls for Rational Debate of Marijuana Laws. But the Police Minister Is Irrational.

" We want a fair and open review. Unfortunately, a large proportion of those affected by the current illicit status of cannabis are too fearful of the law to speak freely and openly on this issue, let alone actually preparing and presenting submissions to the inquiry ", said Les Gray, educational psychologist and CCLR spokesperson.

(MarijuanaNews note: Gray learned this the hard way. He was arrested in May 1989 after appearing on a television program and declaring that he enjoyed the marijuana . His comment sparked four court cases and a national debate on cannabis.

" I decided I wouldn't just admit that I used it. I said, 'Yes thank you, Paul, I enjoy it.' I knew it would antagonise a lot of people, particularly the cannabis cowboys in the police. "

Three days later, police swooped on his houseboat and arrested him for possession. The arrest came five years after Mr Gray, then an Education Department psychologist, was fired from his job for publicly stating his pro-cannabis views.

Gray fought the possession charge, and Judge David McKegg ruled in his favor, saying it struck at the basis of honest debate and freedom of speech that the police had obtained their search warrant as a result of Gray's admission on Holmes.

But the police appealed, and Justice Henry said the dismissal had been exercised on a wrong principle.

Gray failed to overturn the ruling through the Court of Appeal, and ended up back before Judge McKegg.

This time he was fined $100. He resolved to go to jail and fast rather than pay, but an anonymous person came up with the money and he was freed.

Gray is still president of the Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party.)

From
New Zealand Police Minister On the Marijuana Laws:
" My own personal feeling is that it is costing a huge amount of police time at the moment. "
NZ Psychologist Remembers Being Arrested Ten Years Ago For Saying That He Smoked.
– 2 Articles

" By placing a moratorium on cannabis arrests, while the review is conducted, government will the open the doors to widespread and honest public consultation and debate on this issue " he added.

The coalition believes that without honest and open consultation and debate the review process will fail to address the needs of the thousands of New Zealanders affected by the prohibition of cannabis.

Hon. Deborah Morris said, " In a country which prides itself on democracy and the freedom of speech the legal status of cannabis, which entails the threat of arrest and imprisonment, will effectively silence the significant and untapped well of support from people who are in favour of fundamental changes to our failed cannabis policy ".

" The coalition will be doing its utmost to ensure that the views of the hundreds of thousands of cannabis users out there are sought and considered in the review process " added Ms Morris.

ENDS

Contact Les Gray 021 436234 or Hon. Deborah Morris 025 544299

(MarijuanaNews note: Although every large scale hearing on marijuana has arrived at essentially the same conclusion, the New Zealanders are going to have another go at it.

See
A Major Contribution -- Regulate And Tax Cannabis --
Full Text of New Zealand Drug Policy Forum Final Report

This is a mistake. They should be reviewing the disastrous consequences of marijuana prohibition in New Zealand.

In stead, the Select Committee accepted the following terms of reference for the inquiry:

" To inquire into the most effective public health and health promotion strategies to minimise the use and harm associated with cannabis and consequently the most appropriate legal status of cannabis. "

Green Party Marijuana Party Sue Kedgley even said she was " particularly pleased that the focus of the inquiry would be on how the country could minimise the use and the harm of cannabis. "

That is also a mistake. If marijuana was the only drug in the world, then minimizing its use might be a measure of the success of a marijuana policy.

See
Analysis: What If Marijuana Disappeared? By Richard Cowan

But what if marijuana use goes up and heroin addiction goes down? That is precisely what happened in Holland. Of course, marijuana use went up everywhere else, so it does not follow that Dutch teen marijuana went up because of Dutch marijuana policies. The Dutch decline in heroin addiction has not been matched in most other countries, however.

See
Prohibitionist UK Leads Europe In Cannabis Consumption.
More School Children Have Abused Solvents Than In Any Other EU Country.
Following DEAland Policies Gets Them DEAland Results.
and links

So, would the New Zealanders trade an increase in marijuana use for a reduction in heroin addiction? Or alcoholism? Or prescription drug dependence? The fact is that marijuana is far less dangerous than any of the other commonly used drugs.
See
 " Two Drugs Are Quite Enough " NZ Editorial;
Saying Marijuana Is " No Worse Than Alcohol and Tobacco " Won't Work

Moreover, how marijuana is used, that is, the context for its use, is much more important than any headcount of how many people use it.


However, for a free society, the most important question will always " What is the effect of marijuana? "

See
New Zealanders’ Analysis of the Consequences of the Violence of Marijuana Prohibition. Bravo!
That is not the question on the agenda there, so it will be up to the reformers to insist that it be asked.)
